claim: Hst4 protein levels are downregulated upon treatment with MMS in wild-type S. pombe cells.
source: Wild-type (wt) strain (ROP238) containing TAP-tagged Hst4 was grown to 0.5 O.D., treated with 0.015 % MMS and 10 mM HU for 2 hr, respectively, whole cell extracts were prepared and immunoblotted with anti-PAP antibody to detect TAP-tagged Hst4.
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 1A shows reduced Hst4 band intensity after MMS treatment compared to untreated control.

claim: Hst4 protein levels are downregulated upon treatment with HU in wild-type S. pombe cells.
source: Wild-type (wt) strain (ROP238) containing TAP-tagged Hst4 was grown to 0.5 O.D., treated with 0.015 % MMS and 10 mM HU for 2 hr, respectively, whole cell extracts were prepared and immunoblotted with anti-PAP antibody to detect TAP-tagged Hst4.
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 1A shows reduced Hst4 band intensity after HU treatment compared to untreated control.

claim: Hst4 downregulation upon MMS treatment occurs after 90 minutes.
source: wt strain (ROP238) containing TAP-tagged Hst4 was grown to 0.5 O.D., treated with 0.015 % MMS and 10 mM HU, extracts were prepared from cells collected at indicated time points and western blot was performed.
evidence: Western blot time course in Figure 1B shows Hst4 protein levels decrease after 90 min of MMS treatment.

claim: The kinetics of Hst4 downregulation upon HU treatment is similar to MMS treatment.
source: The kinetics of regulation of Hst4 on HU treatment was similar to MMS (Figure 1C).
evidence: Western blot time course in Figure 1C shows similar kinetics of Hst4 degradation with HU as with MMS.

claim: Hst4 downregulation is accelerated by 30 minutes upon MMS treatment during S phase.
source: Interestingly, the downregulation of Hst4 was accelerated by 30 min upon MMS treatment (Figure 1D and E), although MMS slowed S phase progression as shown by the corresponding flow cytometry profiles of cell cycle progression (Figure 1F).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 1D and E shows earlier Hst4 degradation in MMS-treated cells released from G2 arrest compared to untreated cells.

claim: MMS slows S phase progression in synchronized cells.
source: Interestingly, the downregulation of Hst4 was accelerated by 30 min upon MMS treatment (Figure 1D and E), although MMS slowed S phase progression as shown by the corresponding flow cytometry profiles of cell cycle progression (Figure 1F).
evidence: Flow cytometry profiles in Figure 1F show delayed S phase progression in MMS-treated cells compared to untreated cells.

claim: Hst4 levels remain unchanged in G2-arrested cells treated with MMS.
source: The Hst4 levels remained same in cells arrested at G2 phase upon MMS treatment while the asynchronous cells from the same genetic background showed downregulation of Hst4 upon MMS treatment (Figure 1G).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 1G shows stable Hst4 levels in G2-arrested cells treated with MMS, while asynchronous cells show Hst4 degradation.

claim: Hst4 downregulation is dependent on DNA replication.
source: To establish the dependence of regulation of Hst4 on DNA replication-induced stress, cells arrested at the G2 phase were treated with MMS and Hst4 level was examined. The Hst4 levels remained same in cells arrested at G2 phase upon MMS treatment while the asynchronous cells from the same genetic background showed downregulation of Hst4 upon MMS treatment (Figure 1G).
evidence: Comparison of Hst4 levels in G2-arrested versus asynchronous cells treated with MMS shows degradation only occurs during replication.

claim: MMS-induced toxicity is dependent on replication.
source: It has been previously reported that MMS-induced toxicity is dependent on replication and that MMS slows replication fork progression (Cortez, 2005; Stokes et al., 2002).
evidence: Statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: MMS slows replication fork progression.
source: It has been previously reported that MMS-induced toxicity is dependent on replication and that MMS slows replication fork progression (Cortez, 2005; Stokes et al., 2002).
evidence: Statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Hst4 transcript levels are not significantly altered upon MMS treatment.
source: Replication stress does not regulate Hst4 transcriptionally as the transcript level of the gene was not significantly altered upon MMS treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: RT-qPCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A shows no significant change in Hst4 mRNA levels upon MMS treatment.

claim: Hst4 is significantly stabilized in mts2-1 proteasome mutant strain in the absence of MMS.
source: Hst4 was significantly stabilized in mts2-1 strain in the absence or presence of MMS (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 2B shows higher Hst4 levels in mts2-1 mutant compared to wild-type without MMS treatment.

claim: Hst4 is significantly stabilized in mts2-1 proteasome mutant strain in the presence of MMS.
source: Hst4 was significantly stabilized in mts2-1 strain in the absence or presence of MMS (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 2B and cycloheximide chase in Figure 2C show Hst4 stabilization in mts2-1 mutant with MMS treatment.

claim: Hst4 is ubiquitinated in vivo under normal conditions.
source: Hst4 was found to be ubiquitinated under normal as well as upon MMS treatment (Figure 2D).
evidence: Ni-NTA pulldown of His-ubiquitin in Figure 2D shows Hst4 is ubiquitinated in untreated cells.

claim: Hst4 is ubiquitinated in vivo upon MMS treatment.
source: Hst4 was found to be ubiquitinated under normal as well as upon MMS treatment (Figure 2D).
evidence: Ni-NTA pulldown of His-ubiquitin in Figure 2D shows Hst4 is ubiquitinated in MMS-treated cells.

claim: The C-terminal domain of Hst4 (amino acids 353-415) is required for its degradation.
source: The truncated protein was not degraded upon MMS treatment while its full-length counterpart was degraded, confirming the requirement of the C-terminal domain for degradtion of Hst4 (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 2E shows C-terminal deletion mutant (CΔ-Hst4) is not degraded upon MMS treatment while full-length Hst4 is degraded.

claim: The minimum residues required for Hst4 degradation are present between amino acids 352 and 370.
source: We further deleted amino acids 398–415 (T1∆-Hst4) and 371–415 (T2∆-Hst4) and concluded that the minimum residues required for degradation are present between 352 and 370 amino acids as the truncations, T1 and T2 did not lead to complete stabilization of Hst4 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D shows T1Δ and T2Δ truncation mutants are not fully stabilized, indicating the critical region is between amino acids 352-370.

claim: Full-length Hst4 localizes to the nucleus.
source: We have also studied the subcellular localization of FL-Hst4 and C∆-Hst4 and looked at the stability of these proteins upon MMS treatment by immunofluorescence. We observed that both the proteins are localizing perfectly to the nucleus, however, on MMS treatment, FL-Hst4 is degraded while C∆-Hst4 is stabilized (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Immunofluorescence microscopy in Figure 2G shows FL-Hst4-GFP signal colocalizes with nuclear DNA staining.

claim: C-terminal deletion mutant of Hst4 (CΔ-Hst4) localizes to the nucleus.
source: We have also studied the subcellular localization of FL-Hst4 and C∆-Hst4 and looked at the stability of these proteins upon MMS treatment by immunofluorescence. We observed that both the proteins are localizing perfectly to the nucleus, however, on MMS treatment, FL-Hst4 is degraded while C∆-Hst4 is stabilized (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Immunofluorescence microscopy in Figure 2G shows CΔ-Hst4-GFP signal colocalizes with nuclear DNA staining.

claim: Full-length Hst4 is degraded upon MMS treatment as shown by immunofluorescence.
source: We have also studied the subcellular localization of FL-Hst4 and C∆-Hst4 and looked at the stability of these proteins upon MMS treatment by immunofluorescence. We observed that both the proteins are localizing perfectly to the nucleus, however, on MMS treatment, FL-Hst4 is degraded while C∆-Hst4 is stabilized (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Immunofluorescence microscopy in Figure 2G shows loss of FL-Hst4-GFP signal after MMS treatment.

claim: C-terminal deletion mutant of Hst4 (CΔ-Hst4) is stabilized upon MMS treatment as shown by immunofluorescence.
source: We have also studied the subcellular localization of FL-Hst4 and C∆-Hst4 and looked at the stability of these proteins upon MMS treatment by immunofluorescence. We observed that both the proteins are localizing perfectly to the nucleus, however, on MMS treatment, FL-Hst4 is degraded while C∆-Hst4 is stabilized (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Immunofluorescence microscopy in Figure 2G shows persistent CΔ-Hst4-GFP signal after MMS treatment.

claim: Hst4 is phosphorylated at serine residues upon MMS treatment.
source: To test whether Hst4 is phosphorylated upon MMS treatment, TAP-Hst4 was immunoprecipitated from the cells grown in the absence and presence of MMS and the phosphorylation status was checked with phosphoserine antibody. We observed phosphorylation of Hst4 at 1 hr of MMS treatment (Figure 3A).
evidence: Immunoprecipitation followed by western blot with phosphoserine antibody in Figure 3A shows phosphorylated Hst4 band after 1 hr MMS treatment.

claim: Lambda phosphatase treatment of Hst4 results in appearance of a lower mobility form.
source: We also subjected the immunoprecipitated Hst4 sample to lambda phosphatase treatment and observed appearance of a lower mobility form (Figure 3B).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 3B shows shift in Hst4 band mobility after lambda phosphatase treatment, indicating dephosphorylation.

claim: Hst4 is phosphorylated at 60 minutes during unperturbed S phase.
source: Our results show that the phosphorylated band of Hst4 appears at 60 min (Figure 3C).
evidence: Immunoprecipitation followed by western blot with phosphoserine antibody in Figure 3C shows phosphorylated Hst4 band at 60 min timepoint after release from G2 arrest.

claim: Hst4 degradation is not significantly affected in gsk3Δ cells.
source: Since, the C-terminal of Hst4 contained sites of Gsk3-Beta, we checked the level of Hst4 in gsk3Δ cells after MMS treatment. The degradation of Hst4 was not affected significantly in gsk3Δ cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A shows similar Hst4 degradation in gsk3Δ mutant as in wild-type upon MMS treatment.

claim: Hst4 is significantly stable in hsk1-89 mutant after MMS treatment.
source: Hst4 was significantly stable in this mutant even after 4 hr of MMS treatment (Figure 3D).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 3D shows persistent Hst4 levels in hsk1-89 mutant at 2 hr and 4 hr MMS treatment timepoints.

claim: Hst4 is degraded in response to replication stress in mcm4 temperature-sensitive mutant at non-permissive temperature.
source: To check whether the level of Hst4 is altered in mutants where replication initiation is prevented, we checked the level of Hst4 in another replication initiation protein, mcm4 temperature-sensitive mutant (Matsumoto et al., 2010), we found that Hst4 is degraded in response to replication stress in this strain at non-permissive temperature indicating Hsk1 kinase specifically regulates Hst4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B shows Hst4 degradation in mcm4 mutant at non-permissive temperature with MMS treatment.

claim: Wild-type Hsk1 expression rescues Hst4 degradation in hsk1-89 mutant.
source: To further substantiate our results, we complemented hsk1-89 with wild-type Hsk1 and kinase-dead Hsk1 (K129D) cloned in pSLF272 vector and found that Hst4 degradation is rescued upon wild-type Hsk1 expression; however, the kinase-dead Hsk1 is unable to do so (Figure 3E).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 3E shows Hst4 degradation is restored in hsk1-89 mutant complemented with wild-type Hsk1 but not with kinase-dead Hsk1.

claim: Kinase-dead Hsk1 (K129D) is unable to rescue Hst4 degradation in hsk1-89 mutant.
source: To further substantiate our results, we complemented hsk1-89 with wild-type Hsk1 and kinase-dead Hsk1 (K129D) cloned in pSLF272 vector and found that Hst4 degradation is rescued upon wild-type Hsk1 expression; however, the kinase-dead Hsk1 is unable to do so (Figure 3E).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 3E shows Hst4 remains stable in hsk1-89 mutant complemented with kinase-dead K129D-Hsk1.

claim: Dfp1 is not dissociated from chromatin upon replication stress in S. pombe.
source: Our results have shown that neither Dfp1 nor Hsk1 is dissociated from the chromatin upon replication stress; however, we observed a significant reduction of chromatin-bound Hst4 upon MMS treatment as expected due to downregulation (Figure 3F).
evidence: Chromatin fractionation in Figure 3F shows Dfp1 remains in chromatin fraction after MMS treatment.

claim: Hsk1 is not dissociated from chromatin upon replication stress in S. pombe.
source: Our results have shown that neither Dfp1 nor Hsk1 is dissociated from the chromatin upon replication stress; however, we observed a significant reduction of chromatin-bound Hst4 upon MMS treatment as expected due to downregulation (Figure 3F).
evidence: Chromatin fractionation in Figure 3F shows Hsk1 remains in chromatin fraction after MMS treatment.

claim: Chromatin-bound Hst4 is significantly reduced upon MMS treatment.
source: Our results have shown that neither Dfp1 nor Hsk1 is dissociated from the chromatin upon replication stress; however, we observed a significant reduction of chromatin-bound Hst4 upon MMS treatment as expected due to downregulation (Figure 3F).
evidence: Chromatin fractionation in Figure 3F shows reduced Hst4 in chromatin fraction after MMS treatment.

claim: Hst4 is not phosphorylated in hsk1-89 mutant cells upon MMS treatment.
source: Next, we also immunoprecipitated Hst4 from both wild-type and hsk1-89 mutant strain and looked into the phosphorylation status of Hst4 upon MMS treatment. We did not find any phosphorylated band of Hst4 in hsk1-89 cells confirming that Hst4 to be the target of Hsk1 on MMS treatment (Figure 3G).
evidence: Immunoprecipitation followed by western blot with phosphoserine antibody in Figure 3G shows no phosphorylated Hst4 band in hsk1-89 mutant after MMS treatment.

claim: Hst4 interacts with DDK only upon treatment with MMS in wild-type cells after formaldehyde crosslinking.
source: We therefore performed crosslinking by 1 % formaldehyde treatment and observed that Hst4 interacts with DDK only upon treatment with 0.015 % MMS in the wild-type cells (Figure 3H).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation after formaldehyde crosslinking in Figure 3H shows Hst4 interaction with Hsk1 and Dfp1 only in MMS-treated cells.

claim: Hsk1-Dfp1 forms a complex with Hst4 in vitro.
source: Our results show that Hsk1-Dfp1 forms a complex with Hst4 (Figure 3I).
evidence: In vitro binding assay in Figure 3I shows recombinant Hst4 binds to immunoprecipitated Hsk1-Dfp1 complex.

claim: Hsk1 phosphorylates Hst4 in vitro.
source: Finally, we performed an in vitro kinase assay as described in materials and methods and observed that Hsk1 phosphorylates Hst4 as heat inactivation of kinase lead to loss of phosphorylation (Figure 3J).
evidence: In vitro kinase assay in Figure 3J shows phosphorylation of Hst4 by Hsk1, which is lost upon heat inactivation of the kinase.

claim: All four serine residues (S354, S355, S362, and S363) are required for Hst4 degradation.
source: Our results indicate that all four residues are required for degradation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A shows that only the 4SA mutant (all four serines mutated) is fully stabilized, while partial mutations show incomplete stabilization.

claim: Genomically tagged 4SA-Hst4 is stabilized upon MMS treatment.
source: We have made these mutations at the genomic loci, generated TAP-tagged 4SA-Hst4 expressing strain and we found similar stabilization of 4SA-Hst4 upon MMS treatment (Figure 4B) by western blot.
evidence: Western blot in Figure 4B shows 4SA-Hst4 protein levels remain stable after MMS treatment while wild-type Hst4 is degraded.

claim: The half-life of Hst4 is significantly increased in 4SA-hst4 mutant.
source: We have also checked the half-life of Hst4 in wild-type and 4SA-hst4 strains and found that half-life of Hst4 is significantly increased in 4SA-hst4 indicating stabilization (Figure 4C).
evidence: Cycloheximide chase experiment in Figure 4C shows slower degradation of 4SA-Hst4 compared to wild-type Hst4.

claim: Wild-type Hst4 is phosphorylated while 4SA-Hst4 is not phosphorylated.
source: We also went ahead to perform immunoprecipitation to check the phosphorylation status of Hst4 and found that wild-type Hst4 is phosphorylated, however, the 4SA-Hst4 is not phosphorylated (Figure 4D).
evidence: Immunoprecipitation followed by western blot with phosphoserine antibody in Figure 4D shows phosphorylated band for wild-type Hst4 but not for 4SA-Hst4 after MMS treatment.

claim: 4SA-Hst4 loses ubiquitination under untreated conditions.
source: Our results show the loss of ubiquitinated Hst4 upon 4SA-Hst4 expression under untreated as well as treated conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Ni-NTA pulldown of His-ubiquitin in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B shows no ubiquitinated Hst4 band when 4SA-Hst4 is expressed in untreated cells.

claim: 4SA-Hst4 loses ubiquitination under MMS-treated conditions.
source: Our results show the loss of ubiquitinated Hst4 upon 4SA-Hst4 expression under untreated as well as treated conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Ni-NTA pulldown of His-ubiquitin in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B shows no ubiquitinated Hst4 band when 4SA-Hst4 is expressed in MMS-treated cells.

claim: Hsk1 does not phosphorylate 4SA-Hst4 in vitro.
source: Finally, we performed an in vitro phosphorylation assay using γ-P32 ATP, purified mutated recombinant Hst4 proteins expressed in BL21 cells and Hsk1 immunoprecipitated from S. pombe cells and no phosphorylation was observed when 4SA-Hst4 was used as substrate (Figure 4E).
evidence: In vitro kinase assay with radioactive ATP in Figure 4E shows no phosphorylation signal for 4SA-Hst4 substrate while full-length Hst4 is phosphorylated.

claim: Cells expressing 4SA-hst4 are slow growing.
source: As shown in Figure 4F, we found that cells expressing 4SA-hst4 are slow growing and sensitive to replication stress as compared to wild-type.
evidence: Spot assay in Figure 4F shows reduced colony size for 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type on YES plates.

claim: Cells expressing 4SA-hst4 are sensitive to MMS.
source: As shown in Figure 4F, we found that cells expressing 4SA-hst4 are slow growing and sensitive to replication stress as compared to wild-type.
evidence: Spot assay in Figure 4F shows reduced growth of 4SA-hst4 mutant on MMS-containing plates compared to wild-type.

claim: Cells expressing 4SA-hst4 are sensitive to HU.
source: As shown in Figure 4F, we found that cells expressing 4SA-hst4 are slow growing and sensitive to replication stress as compared to wild-type.
evidence: Spot assay in Figure 4F shows reduced growth of 4SA-hst4 mutant on HU-containing plates compared to wild-type.

claim: 4SA-hst4 mutant has significant growth recovery defect after MMS treatment.
source: The results in Figure 4G and H show that 4SA-hst4 has significant growth recovery defect as compared to wild-type.
evidence: Colony formation assay in Figure 4G shows lower percent survival of 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type after MMS treatment and washout.

claim: 4SA-hst4 mutant has significant growth recovery defect after HU treatment.
source: The results in Figure 4G and H show that 4SA-hst4 has significant growth recovery defect as compared to wild-type.
evidence: Colony formation assay in Figure 4H shows lower percent survival of 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type after HU treatment and washout.

claim: Treatment with HU leads to more sensitivity and recovery defects in 4SA-hst4 mutant cells than treatment with MMS.
source: We have observed that treatment with HU leads to more sensitivity and recovery defects in 4SA-hst4 mutant cells than on treatment with MMS.
evidence: Comparison of survival curves in Figure 4G and 4H shows greater reduction in survival for 4SA-hst4 mutant with HU than with MMS.

claim: Hst4 is significantly stabilized in pof3Δ cells.
source: We found that Hst4 was significantly stabilized in the pof3Δ cells (Figure 5A).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 5A shows higher Hst4 levels in pof3Δ mutant compared to wild-type after MMS treatment.

claim: The half-life of Hst4 is significantly increased in pof3Δ compared to wild-type.
source: Further, we have examined the half-life of Hst4 in the pof3Δ using CHX in the presence of MMS and observed that the half life of Hst4 was significantly increased in pof3Δ compared to wild-type (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Cycloheximide chase experiment in Figure 5B shows slower Hst4 degradation in pof3Δ mutant compared to wild-type with MMS treatment.

claim: Hst4 is significantly stabilized in skp1-94 mutant.
source: Next, we confirmed the role of SCFpof3 in the degradation of Hst4 by checking the levels of Hst4 in skp1-94 which is specifically defective in interaction with Pof3 (Roseaulin et al., 2013a). Our results show that Hst4 is significantly stabilized in skp1-94 (Figure 5C).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 5C shows higher Hst4 levels in skp1-94 mutant compared to wild-type after MMS treatment.

claim: Hst4 is not stabilized in skp1-A4 strain.
source: We did not observe stabilization of Hst4 in the skp1-A4 strain where Skp1 interaction with Pof3 is intact (Lehmann et al., 2004; Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C shows Hst4 degradation in skp1-A4 mutant similar to wild-type after MMS treatment.

claim: Hst4 interacts with Pof3 in mts2-1 strain without replication stress.
source: We observed that Hst4 interacts with Pof3 in mts2-1 strain without replication stress as well as upon MMS treatment (Figure 5D).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation in Figure 5D shows Hst4 co-precipitates with HA-Pof3 in mts2-1 cells without MMS treatment.

claim: Hst4 interacts with Pof3 in mts2-1 strain upon MMS treatment.
source: We observed that Hst4 interacts with Pof3 in mts2-1 strain without replication stress as well as upon MMS treatment (Figure 5D).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation in Figure 5D shows Hst4 co-precipitates with HA-Pof3 in mts2-1 cells with MMS treatment.

claim: Pof3 interacts with Hst4 only in the presence of MMS in wild-type cells.
source: We observed that pof3 interacts with Hst4 only in the presence of MMS in the wild-type cells upon 1 hr of treatment (Figure 5E).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation in Figure 5E shows Hst4 co-precipitates with HA-Pof3 only after 1 hr MMS treatment in wild-type cells.

claim: Pof3 protein levels are upregulated upon MMS treatment in wild-type cells.
source: Interestingly, we found that the Pof3 protein levels were upregulated upon MMS and HU treatment in wild-type cells (Figure 5F).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 5F shows increased Pof3 band intensity after MMS treatment compared to untreated control.

claim: Pof3 protein levels are upregulated upon HU treatment in wild-type cells.
source: Interestingly, we found that the Pof3 protein levels were upregulated upon MMS and HU treatment in wild-type cells (Figure 5F).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 5F shows increased Pof3 band intensity after HU treatment compared to untreated control.

claim: 4SA-hst4 mutant shows high DNA fragmentation after 6 hours of HU treatment.
source: We found a high amount of DNA fragmentation and septated cells shown by DNA staining after 6 hr of HU treatment indicating aberrant mitosis while wild-type cells were arrested, as indicated by the appearance of elongated, uninucleate cells without septa (Figure 6A).
evidence: Microscopy images in Figure 6A show fragmented DNA in 4SA-hst4 mutant cells after 6 hr HU treatment.

claim: 4SA-hst4 mutant shows septated cells after 6 hours of HU treatment indicating aberrant mitosis.
source: We found a high amount of DNA fragmentation and septated cells shown by DNA staining after 6 hr of HU treatment indicating aberrant mitosis while wild-type cells were arrested, as indicated by the appearance of elongated, uninucleate cells without septa (Figure 6A).
evidence: Microscopy images in Figure 6A show septated cells in 4SA-hst4 mutant after 6 hr HU treatment, which is interpreted as aberrant mitosis.

claim: Wild-type cells are arrested after 6 hours of HU treatment as indicated by elongated, uninucleate cells without septa.
source: We found a high amount of DNA fragmentation and septated cells shown by DNA staining after 6 hr of HU treatment indicating aberrant mitosis while wild-type cells were arrested, as indicated by the appearance of elongated, uninucleate cells without septa (Figure 6A).
evidence: Microscopy images in Figure 6A show elongated cells without septa in wild-type after 6 hr HU treatment.

claim: 4SA-hst4 mutant shows delayed S-phase progression.
source: Since, we observed slow growth and loss of viability upon mutation of 4SA-hst4, we studied the cell cycle progression upon the G2 block and release into the S phase in this mutant. We observed a delay in S-phase progression in this mutant (Figure 6B).
evidence: Flow cytometry profiles in Figure 6B show slower progression through S phase in 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type after release from G2 arrest.

claim: H2A phosphorylation is reduced by 3 hours during recovery in wild-type cells.
source: We found that H2A phosphorylation was reduced by 3 hr during recovery in wild-type whereas it persists in 4SA-hst4 (Figure 6C).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 6C shows decreased H2A-P signal at 3 hr recovery timepoint in wild-type cells.

claim: H2A phosphorylation persists in 4SA-hst4 mutant during recovery from MMS treatment.
source: We found that H2A phosphorylation was reduced by 3 hr during recovery in wild-type whereas it persists in 4SA-hst4 (Figure 6C).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 6C shows sustained H2A-P signal at 3 hr recovery timepoint in 4SA-hst4 mutant cells.

claim: Wild-type cells finish S-phase and resume cell cycle progression after HU-induced cell cycle arrest.
source: We observed that the wild-type cells finished S-phase and resumed cell cycle progression, however, the 4SA-hst4 showed delayed S-phase progression which further confirms the inability of this mutant to recover from HU-induced replication stress (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Flow cytometry profiles in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A show wild-type cells complete S phase and progress through cell cycle after HU washout.

claim: 4SA-hst4 mutant shows delayed S-phase progression after HU-induced cell cycle arrest.
source: We observed that the wild-type cells finished S-phase and resumed cell cycle progression, however, the 4SA-hst4 showed delayed S-phase progression which further confirms the inability of this mutant to recover from HU-induced replication stress (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Flow cytometry profiles in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A show 4SA-hst4 mutant cells remain in S phase longer after HU washout compared to wild-type.

claim: The IdU:CldU ratio is significantly lower in 4SA-hst4 than in wild-type indicating defective fork restart.
source: The results in Figure 6D and E show that the IdU:CldU ratio is significantly lower in 4SA-hst4 than that in wild-type indicating the critical need for degradation of Hst4 for fork restart.
evidence: Dual nucleotide analog labeling experiment quantified in Figure 6E shows lower IdU:CldU ratio in 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type, indicating fewer forks restart after HU treatment.

claim: Initial replication foci detected by CldU are similar in both wild-type and 4SA-hst4.
source: The initial replication foci detected by CldU was found to be similar in both wild-type and 4SA-hst4 implying that the early replication is not hampered in the 4SA-hst4 mutant.
evidence: Immunofluorescence images in Figure 6D show similar CldU foci numbers in wild-type and 4SA-hst4 mutant before HU treatment.

claim: Only 25 percent of 4SA-hst4 cells recover from MMS treatment in S phase as measured by BrdU incorporation.
source: We have performed the restart efficiency using single analog labeling by BrdU post MMS treatment recovery in the S phase and observed that only 25 percent of cells were recovered from the stress whereas wild-type cells efficiently recovered and restarted (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: BrdU incorporation assay quantified in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C shows approximately 25% BrdU-positive cells in 4SA-hst4 mutant after MMS recovery.

claim: Wild-type cells efficiently recover and restart replication after MMS treatment as measured by BrdU incorporation.
source: We have performed the restart efficiency using single analog labeling by BrdU post MMS treatment recovery in the S phase and observed that only 25 percent of cells were recovered from the stress whereas wild-type cells efficiently recovered and restarted (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: BrdU incorporation assay quantified in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C shows approximately 45% BrdU-positive cells in wild-type after MMS recovery.

claim: swi1Δhst4Δ double mutant is synthetic lethal.
source: We made double mutants of swi1∆hst4∆ and swi3∆hst4∆ and found that the combination is synthetic lethal as we could not recover spores (Figure 7A).
evidence: Tetrad dissection in Figure 7A shows no viable spores with both swi1Δ and hst4Δ markers.

claim: swi3Δhst4Δ double mutant is synthetic lethal.
source: We made double mutants of swi1∆hst4∆ and swi3∆hst4∆ and found that the combination is synthetic lethal as we could not recover spores (Figure 7A).
evidence: Tetrad dissection in Figure 7A shows no viable spores with both swi3Δ and hst4Δ markers.

claim: Hst4 physically interacts with Swi1 in vitro.
source: To check whether there is physical interaction between Hst4 and Swi1-Swi3, Swi1-FLAG and Swi3-FLAG proteins were immunoprecipitated from untreated or MMS treated fission yeast cells and incubated with recombinant Fl-Hst4. We observed that Hst4 physically interacts with Swi1 and Swi3 in vitro (Figure 7B).
evidence: In vitro binding assay in Figure 7B shows recombinant Hst4 binds to immunoprecipitated Swi1-FLAG.

claim: Hst4 physically interacts with Swi3 in vitro.
source: To check whether there is physical interaction between Hst4 and Swi1-Swi3, Swi1-FLAG and Swi3-FLAG proteins were immunoprecipitated from untreated or MMS treated fission yeast cells and incubated with recombinant Fl-Hst4. We observed that Hst4 physically interacts with Swi1 and Swi3 in vitro (Figure 7B).
evidence: In vitro binding assay in Figure 7B shows recombinant Hst4 binds to immunoprecipitated Swi3-FLAG.

claim: Swi1 is significantly overexpressed in 4SA-hst4 mutant.
source: We checked the whole cell levels of FPC in 4SA-hst4 mutant and interestingly found that Swi1 is significantly overexpressed when Hst4 was not degraded (Figure 7C).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 7C shows increased Swi1 band intensity in 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type.

claim: Mcl1 is overexpressed in 4SA-hst4 mutant.
source: Mcl1, the homolog of human And-1 is also a part of FPC in higher eukaryotes. Therefore, we looked at the levels of Mcl1 and overexpression of Mcl1 was observed.
evidence: Western blot in Figure 7C shows increased Mcl1 band intensity in 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type.

claim: Mrc1 is upregulated in 4SA-hst4 strain.
source: We have observed that Mrc1 is also upregulated in the 4SA-hst4 strain (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D shows increased Mrc1 band intensity in 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type.

claim: PCNA expression is not altered in 4SA-hst4 strain upon MMS treatment.
source: We have also looked at the expression of PCNA, which is a clamp protein, crucial for DNA replication. We did not find altered expression of PCNA in 4SA-hst4 strain upon treatment with both MMS and HU which shows specific regulation of Swi1 and Mcl1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E shows similar PCNA band intensity in wild-type and 4SA-hst4 mutant with MMS treatment.

claim: PCNA expression is not altered in 4SA-hst4 strain upon HU treatment.
source: We have also looked at the expression of PCNA, which is a clamp protein, crucial for DNA replication. We did not find altered expression of PCNA in 4SA-hst4 strain upon treatment with both MMS and HU which shows specific regulation of Swi1 and Mcl1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 7—figure supplement 1F shows similar PCNA band intensity in wild-type and 4SA-hst4 mutant with HU treatment.

claim: Chromatin-associated Swi1 is reduced in 4SA-hst4 strain.
source: We next checked the chromatin association of FPC in the 4SA-hst4 strain and found that there is reduced level of Swi1 and Mcl1 at the chromatin when Hst4 is not degraded. (Figure 7D).
evidence: Chromatin fractionation in Figure 7D shows decreased Swi1 in chromatin fraction of 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type after HU treatment.

claim: Chromatin-associated Mcl1 is reduced in 4SA-hst4 strain.
source: We next checked the chromatin association of FPC in the 4SA-hst4 strain and found that there is reduced level of Swi1 and Mcl1 at the chromatin when Hst4 is not degraded. (Figure 7D).
evidence: Chromatin fractionation in Figure 7D shows decreased Mcl1 in chromatin fraction of 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type after HU treatment.

claim: Chromatin-enriched Mcl1 is less enriched in 4SA-hst4 strain as shown by co-immunoprecipitation.
source: We confirmed our results by performing co-immunoprecipitation of chromatin enriched Mcl1, found that these proteins are less enriched in 4SA-hst4 strain (Figure 7E).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation from chromatin fraction in Figure 7E shows reduced Mcl1 and Swi1 co-precipitating in 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type after HU treatment.

claim: Intra-S phase checkpoint activation is normal in 4SA-hst4 mutant.
source: We found that intra-S phase activation is normal in both wild-type and 4SA-hst4 strain (Figure 7Fand G).
evidence: Cds1 kinase assay in Figure 7F and quantification in Figure 7G show similar Cds1 activity in wild-type and 4SA-hst4 mutant after MMS treatment.

claim: H3K56 acetylation is significantly reduced in 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type in untreated conditions.
source: We determined the H3K56 acetylation status in 4SA-hst4 mutant and found that H3K56ac is significantly reduced in this mutant as compared to wild-type in both untreated and upon MMS treatment (Figure 8A).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 8A shows decreased H3K56ac band intensity in 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type without MMS treatment.

claim: H3K56 acetylation is significantly reduced in 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type upon MMS treatment.
source: We determined the H3K56 acetylation status in 4SA-hst4 mutant and found that H3K56ac is significantly reduced in this mutant as compared to wild-type in both untreated and upon MMS treatment (Figure 8A).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 8A shows decreased H3K56ac band intensity in 4SA-hst4 mutant compared to wild-type with MMS treatment.

claim: Whole cell levels of FPC are upregulated in H3K56R mutant.
source: We next checked the whole cell levels of FPC in H3K56R mutants, which mimic hypoacetylation (Haldar and Kamakaka, 2008). We found that the whole cell levels of FPC are also upregulated in H3K56R mutant indicating the regulation of FPC could be dependent upon H3K56 acetylation (Figure 8B).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 8B shows increased Swi1 and Mcl1 band intensity in H3K56R mutant compared to wild-type.

claim: Chromatin-associated Swi1 is reduced in H3K56R mutant.
source: To further confirm that the reduced chromatin association of FPC at the chromatin is dependent upon H3K56ac, we checked the chromatin association of FPC in the H3K56R mutant. We observed lesser enrichment of Swi1 and Mcl1 at the chromatin in these mutants (Figure 8C).
evidence: Chromatin fractionation in Figure 8C shows decreased Swi1 in chromatin fraction of H3K56R mutant compared to wild-type after HU treatment.

claim: Chromatin-associated Mcl1 is reduced in H3K56R mutant.
source: To further confirm that the reduced chromatin association of FPC at the chromatin is dependent upon H3K56ac, we checked the chromatin association of FPC in the H3K56R mutant. We observed lesser enrichment of Swi1 and Mcl1 at the chromatin in these mutants (Figure 8C).
evidence: Chromatin fractionation in Figure 8C shows decreased Mcl1 in chromatin fraction of H3K56R mutant compared to wild-type after HU treatment.

claim: H3K56 acetylation is drastically reduced in hsk1-89 strain.
source: We then checked the acetylation status of H3K56 under conditions where Hst4 was found to be stabilized that is in the absence of hsk1 and pof3. Our results indicate that H3K56ac is drastically reduced in both hsk1-89 and pof3∆ strains as a consequence of constitutive Hst4 expression in these strains (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A shows decreased H3K56ac band intensity in hsk1-89 mutant compared to wild-type.

claim: H3K56 acetylation is drastically reduced in pof3Δ strain.
source: We then checked the acetylation status of H3K56 under conditions where Hst4 was found to be stabilized that is in the absence of hsk1 and pof3. Our results indicate that H3K56ac is drastically reduced in both hsk1-89 and pof3∆ strains as a consequence of constitutive Hst4 expression in these strains (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B shows decreased H3K56ac band intensity in pof3Δ mutant compared to wild-type with MMS treatment.

claim: Upon Asf1a knockdown in U2OS cells, there is a significant reduction of Timeless.
source: To check the conservation of regulation of FPC, we studied the levels of FPC upon knock down of Asf1a which regulates H3K56ac in the human U2OS cell line. We performed western blot to study the whole cell levels of FPC. Our results show that upon Asf1a knock down, there was a significant reduction of FPC components Tim, Tipin, and And-1 (Figure 8D).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 8D shows decreased Timeless band intensity in Asf1a siRNA-treated U2OS cells compared to scramble control.

claim: Upon Asf1a knockdown in U2OS cells, there is a significant reduction of Tipin.
source: To check the conservation of regulation of FPC, we studied the levels of FPC upon knock down of Asf1a which regulates H3K56ac in the human U2OS cell line. We performed western blot to study the whole cell levels of FPC. Our results show that upon Asf1a knock down, there was a significant reduction of FPC components Tim, Tipin, and And-1 (Figure 8D).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 8D shows decreased Tipin band intensity in Asf1a siRNA-treated U2OS cells compared to scramble control.

claim: Upon Asf1a knockdown in U2OS cells, there is a significant reduction of And-1.
source: To check the conservation of regulation of FPC, we studied the levels of FPC upon knock down of Asf1a which regulates H3K56ac in the human U2OS cell line. We performed western blot to study the whole cell levels of FPC. Our results show that upon Asf1a knock down, there was a significant reduction of FPC components Tim, Tipin, and And-1 (Figure 8D).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 8D shows decreased And-1 band intensity in Asf1a siRNA-treated U2OS cells compared to scramble control.

claim: Sirtuin 2 levels are not altered upon Asf1a knockdown in U2OS cells.
source: Since, H3K56ac is regulated by sirtuins, we checked the level of Sirtuin 2 and found that level of Sirtuin 2 was not altered upon Asf1 knock down.
evidence: Western blot in Figure 8D shows similar Sirtuin 2 band intensity in Asf1a siRNA-treated and scramble control U2OS cells.

claim: Chromatin-bound Timeless is significantly decreased upon Asf1a knockdown in U2OS cells.
source: To confirm these results, we performed chromatin fractionation upon Asf1a knock down in U2OS cells. Our results revealed a significant decrease in the chromatin-bound Tim and And-1 consistent with the reduction in whole cell levels (Figure 8E).
evidence: Chromatin fractionation in Figure 8E shows decreased Timeless in chromatin fraction of Asf1a siRNA-treated U2OS cells compared to scramble control.

claim: Chromatin-bound And-1 is significantly decreased upon Asf1a knockdown in U2OS cells.
source: To confirm these results, we performed chromatin fractionation upon Asf1a knock down in U2OS cells. Our results revealed a significant decrease in the chromatin-bound Tim and And-1 consistent with the reduction in whole cell levels (Figure 8E).
evidence: Chromatin fractionation in Figure 8E shows decreased And-1 in chromatin fraction of Asf1a siRNA-treated U2OS cells compared to scramble control.

claim: DDK/Hsk1 phosphorylates sirtuin Hst4 upon replication stress at C-terminal serine residues.
source: Here, we show that fission yeast DDK/Hsk1 phosphorylates sirtuin, Hst4 upon replication stress at C-terminal serine residues.
evidence: Multiple experiments including in vitro kinase assays, phosphorylation detection, and mutational analysis support this claim.

claim: Phosphorylation of Hst4 by DDK marks it for degradation via the ubiquitin ligase SCFpof3.
source: Phosphorylation of Hst4 by DDK marks it for degradation via the ubiquitin ligase SCFpof3.
evidence: Experiments showing Hst4 stabilization in pof3Δ and skp1-94 mutants, ubiquitination assays, and interaction studies support this claim.

claim: Phosphorylation-defective hst4 mutant (4SA-hst4) displays defective recovery from replication stress.
source: Phosphorylation-defective hst4 mutant (4SA-hst4) displays defective recovery from replication stress, faulty fork restart, slow S-phase progression and decreased viability.
evidence: Multiple phenotypic assays including survival assays, cell cycle analysis, and fork restart experiments demonstrate these defects.

claim: Phosphorylation-defective hst4 mutant (4SA-hst4) displays faulty fork restart.
source: Phosphorylation-defective hst4 mutant (4SA-hst4) displays defective recovery from replication stress, faulty fork restart, slow S-phase progression and decreased viability.
evidence: Dual nucleotide analog labeling experiments show reduced fork restart in 4SA-hst4 mutant.

claim: Phosphorylation-defective hst4 mutant (4SA-hst4) displays slow S-phase progression.
source: Phosphorylation-defective hst4 mutant (4SA-hst4) displays defective recovery from replication stress, faulty fork restart, slow S-phase progression and decreased viability.
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shows delayed S phase progression in 4SA-hst4 mutant.

claim: Phosphorylation-defective hst4 mutant (4SA-hst4) displays decreased viability.
source: Phosphorylation-defective hst4 mutant (4SA-hst4) displays defective recovery from replication stress, faulty fork restart, slow S-phase progression and decreased viability.
evidence: Survival assays and spot assays show reduced viability of 4SA-hst4 mutant under replication stress.

claim: The recruitment of FPC components Swi1 and Mcl1 to chromatin is compromised in the 4SA-hst4 mutant.
source: We found that the recruitment of FPC components, Swi1 and Mcl1 to the chromatin is compromised in the 4SA-hst4 mutant, although whole cell levels increased.
evidence: Chromatin fractionation experiments show reduced chromatin-associated Swi1 and Mcl1 in 4SA-hst4 mutant despite increased whole cell levels.

claim: Whole cell levels of Swi1 and Mcl1 are increased in the 4SA-hst4 mutant.
source: We found that the recruitment of FPC components, Swi1 and Mcl1 to the chromatin is compromised in the 4SA-hst4 mutant, although whole cell levels increased.
evidence: Western blot analysis shows increased Swi1 and Mcl1 protein levels in 4SA-hst4 mutant whole cell extracts.

claim: The defects in 4SA-hst4 mutant are dependent upon H3K56ac.
source: These defects are dependent upon H3K56ac and independent of intra S-phase checkpoint activation.
evidence: H3K56R mutant phenocopies 4SA-hst4 defects in FPC chromatin association, and H3K56ac levels are reduced in 4SA-hst4 mutant.

claim: The defects in 4SA-hst4 mutant are independent of intra S-phase checkpoint activation.
source: These defects are dependent upon H3K56ac and independent of intra S-phase checkpoint activation.
evidence: Cds1 kinase assay shows normal checkpoint activation in 4SA-hst4 mutant.

claim: There is conservation of H3K56ac-dependent regulation of Timeless, Tipin, and And-1 in human cells.
source: Finally, we show conservation of H3K56ac-dependent regulation of Timeless, Tipin, and And-1 in human cells.
evidence: Asf1a knockdown in U2OS cells reduces FPC component levels and chromatin association, similar to effects seen in yeast mutants.

claim: Degradation of Hst4 via DDK increases H3K56ac.
source: We propose that degradation of Hst4 via DDK increases H3K56ac, changing the chromatin state in the vicinity of stalled forks facilitating recruitment and function of FPC.
evidence: H3K56ac levels are reduced when Hst4 is stabilized (in 4SA-hst4, hsk1-89, and pof3Δ mutants), and FPC chromatin association is compromised under these conditions.

claim: Increased H3K56ac changes the chromatin state in the vicinity of stalled forks.
source: We propose that degradation of Hst4 via DDK increases H3K56ac, changing the chromatin state in the vicinity of stalled forks facilitating recruitment and function of FPC.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the observed correlation between H3K56ac levels and FPC chromatin association.

claim: Changed chromatin state facilitates recruitment and function of FPC at stalled forks.
source: We propose that degradation of Hst4 via DDK increases H3K56ac, changing the chromatin state in the vicinity of stalled forks facilitating recruitment and function of FPC.
evidence: FPC chromatin association is reduced when H3K56ac is low (in 4SA-hst4 and H3K56R mutants), supporting this proposed mechanism.

claim: DDK has a crucial role in the regulation of replication stress response.
source: Overall, this study identified a crucial role of DDK and FPC in the regulation of replication stress response with implications in cancer therapeutics.
evidence: The study demonstrates DDK phosphorylates Hst4 to regulate FPC function during replication stress.

claim: FPC has a crucial role in the regulation of replication stress response.
source: Overall, this study identified a crucial role of DDK and FPC in the regulation of replication stress response with implications in cancer therapeutics.
evidence: The study shows FPC components are essential for fork stability and their regulation is conserved in human cells where they are overexpressed in cancers.

claim: The findings have implications in cancer therapeutics.
source: Overall, this study identified a crucial role of DDK and FPC in the regulation of replication stress response with implications in cancer therapeutics.
evidence: FPC components are known to be upregulated in cancers, and this study identifies a regulatory mechanism that could be therapeutically targeted.
